prerequisites: Competencies developed in the courses "Mathematical Analysis 1" and "Linear Algebra and Elements of Geometry"

learning_outcomes.text: Know and be able to apply numerical methods for finding function zeros, interpolation, and numerical integration.
Understand and use numerical methods for solving ordinary differential equations.
Acquire basic notions of numerical optimization, with particular reference to gradient-based methods.
Develop a critical approach in the selection, application, and evaluation of numerical methods.
Refine mathematical language and the ability to formulate and solve problems rigorously.
Understand and be able to discuss the main methods of numerical series analysis and know the basics of function series.
Master theoretical solution techniques for ordinary differential equations.
Develop skills in multivariable real calculus.

syllabus_topics: Numerical methods for root finding, including the bisection method, fixed-point iteration, Newton's method.
Introduction to numerical integration, including the rectangle, trapezoidal, and Cavalieri-Simpson rules.
One-step numerical methods for ordinary differential equations, with particular emphasis on the forward Euler method.
Introduction to optimization, including unconstrained optimization by gradient descent methods and constrained optimization by the method of Lagrange multipliers.
Series: numerical series and related classical intuitions, convergence, series with positive terms, series with alternating signs, introduction to function series with applications.
Ordinary differential equations: basic notions, first-order equations, second-order linear equations.

Functions of several variables: elementary properties of R^n, limits and continuity, partial derivatives, gradient, tangent plane, differentiability and directional derivatives, higher-order derivatives and Hessian matrix, Taylor polynomials, introduction to partial differential equations with applications, double integrals.

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (mandatory for a grade above 27)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a mandatory written exam and an optional oral exam. The oral exam is mandatory to achieve a grade above 27/30. A grade of 27/30 is the maximum without the oral exam. Passing grades range from 18/30 (sufficient) to 30 cum laude (excellent with distinction).
bibliography: M. Bertsch, R. Dal Passo and L. Giacomelli, Analisi matematica, McGraw-Hill
Slides/notes will be made available by the lecturer
